column12: Judgement on the comparator. Adakveo is the one branded disease-modifying drug on the US market labelled to cut sickle cell crises (openFDA label BLA761128, effective 2026-06-04), and a crisis rate is a co-primary endpoint of HIBISCUS. Part B is its main channel: its 2025 Part D row is 84 beneficiaries at $65,238.48 (quarterly companion 4ff7c618-4e40-483a-b390-c8a58c94fa15), against 424 in Part B. The 2024 basis was $62,060. No oral comparator in the same patients has a 2025 row: Pfizer withdrew Oxbryta in September 2024 (Q4 2024 8-K exhibit 99, 0000078003-25-000017), and Endari, a glutamine powder, reads $12,644.90 in Part D 2025. Mitapivat, the first PKR activator, is not approved in sickle cell disease (openFDA labels NDA216196: Pyrukynd in PK deficiency, Aqvesme in thalassaemia), and its Part D figure of $242,256.47 a beneficiary in 2025 is an ultra-rare price, not one for a population of 100,000. The net here, $57,937, sits within 2% of Oxbryta's measured net on the osivelotor seed ($56,990). The case against: an infused monthly antibody prices an oral daily pill

column12: Why the age cut alone: sickle cell labels name age and disease and nothing else. HIBISCUS's own entry window (registry: 2 or more crises in 12 months, no more than 15, haemoglobin 5.5 to 10.5 g/dL, age 12 to 65) is 6.8% of patients on the osivelotor seed's arithmetic, and that pool cannot hold the patients a sickle cell disease-modifier has actually reached: Oxbryta sold $323mm in the US in 2023 (Pfizer Q4 2024 8-K exhibit 99, 0000078003-25-000017), about 5,700 patients at its own net, more than 80% of a 6,800 pool, and with 67% stopping each year it started far more than that. The case for lower: Shah's cohort is Medicaid, where children are over-represented, so the adult share of all US patients is likely higher, not lower; payers may restrict to recurrent crises as they do for Adakveo
